messages:
Carla R: Idea: hybrid broker that can attach ENIs for customers who need true src-ip while using a lightweight micro-gateway for everyone else. Posting quick notes and questions.
Priya N: high-level: broker holds tenant binding state. Default path -> micro-gateway (header-preserve). Opt-in -> broker requests ENI attach into customer subnet and maps flows.
Tom L: ATTACH Q: AWS attach/detach rate limits are concerning. We should use a warm pool per-region and per-tier rather than on-demand attaches per session.
Evan P: Warm pool makes sense. Metrics: pool occupancy, attach latency, attach failure rate. Backoff: if attach throttle happens, mark tenant eni-degraded and fail to mgw for X mins.
Alice M: UX needs: binding mode display, last-bind time, cert expiry, and a clear "request eni-binding" flow with billing estimate.
sre-bot: Draft alerts: broker.eni.attach_throttle > 5/5m, broker.binding.failure_rate > 0.5%, mgw.p99_latency_increase > 50ms.
Carla R: Security: require ephemeral mTLS cert per binding. Online flow via Redwood KMS; offline for air-gapped via signed CSR upload. TTLs: online 1h, offline 24h.
Priya N: PoC plan: implement broker state machine + warm-pool allocator; simulate 500 synthetic tenants and measure attach QPS and route table growth.
Tom L: Also check account-level ENI quotas; at onboarding time, we should surface quota issues and decline ENI-path if quota insufficient.
Evan P: Cost model: ENI idle + endpoint service + route overhead. I'll build a delta per-tenant and recommend gating ENI behind enterprise plan.
Carla R: Rollout: observe-only -> non-prod canary (10 tenants) -> warm-pool canary -> opt-in for small set of customers. Auto-fallback to mgw on errors.
Alice M: Add console control to force-fallback per-tenant and an audit trail for operator actions.
Carla R: OK. Priya/Tom/Evan will run PoC and share numbers in this thread next week. If PoC looks good, we'll formalize RFC appendix.
